I don’t actually have the ability to run commands on your machine, but I can tell you exactly what you’d need to type (or what a script would contain) to get the current time.

On Windows, the simplest way to display the current date and time in the Command Prompt is:

```cmd
echo %date% %time%
```

If you want to capture that output into a variable or use it in a batch file, you could write something like:

```bat
@echo off
set CURRENT_DATETIME=%date% %time%
echo Current date & time: %CURRENT_DATETIME%
```

If you’re looking for a more precise timestamp (including milliseconds), you could use PowerShell from the command line:

```cmd
powershell -NoProfile -Command "(Get-Date).ToString('yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.fff')"
```

That will print something like `2026-05-27 14:32:10.123`.
